quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When approaching a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is crossing. Always let them cross first.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers to watch for people crossing the street.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane must move to another lane.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe if you take the right amount.
Prescription medicines are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines often cause drowsiness. Always check how a medicine affects you before driving.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the wet air and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving behind another car at night, you should:

options.text: Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away.

questions.explanation: Always use low beams when following another driver. High beams shine in their mirrors and can blind them.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights anytime you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: Why is winter driving more dangerous than other seasons?

options.text: Ice, snow, fog, and freezing temperatures affect the roads.
There are more hours of darkness.

questions.explanation: Winter brings many hazards: fog, rain, snow, sleet, ice, and longer dark hours. Good drivers prepare for these conditions.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. It can reduce visibility and push any vehicle sideways on the road.

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is raised. Then make sure no children are crossing before you go.

questions.question: The correct way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, then move toward the center before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal your turn, slow down, and stay in the right lane close to the curb as you turn right.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: The side with the broken line can pass.
The side with the solid line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side with the broken line can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Slowing down just to look at accidents or unusual sights:
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or other distractions. This behavior, called "rubbernecking," causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of your seat belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: When a cyclist is turning left:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut across all lanes.
They may wait on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Cyclists ride with traffic on the road. Expect to see cyclists using the left lane when they turn left.

questions.question: When entering the highway on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Enter the right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the road shoulder to speed up.
Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic to enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp, wait until you find a gap in traffic. Speed up and merge into that gap. Wait while stopped if needed until a safe gap appears.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn and guide you through the work zone.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your wheels?
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the road edge when parking uphill or downhill with no curb. This way, if your brakes fail, the vehicle rolls away from traffic.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have and show all three: your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You need all three when driving.

questions.question: On a highway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop.

questions.explanation: On highways, watch for changes in traffic ahead. Look for signals from other drivers, merging vehicles, and changing road conditions. Plan ahead.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: When must drivers stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at the driver.
Only if the pedestrians are not using their phone.

questions.explanation: Always stop at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You can proceed only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering the interstate. Use the acceleration lane to speed up and match the traffic flow, then merge smoothly.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your safety belt, and secure any loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red eight-sided sign means stop.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You may turn after a complete stop.
You may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means do not go in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed is 55 mph in good conditions.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph in good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for this road. You may drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange is used for construction and maintenance areas.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions and no one can pass.

questions.question: You must use low beam headlights when:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off precipitation and make it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights to use with low beams.

questions.question: When leaving a parking spot at a curb to enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can reach traffic speed.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can reach traffic speed.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to speed up to match other traffic.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for someone to step out or a car to pull out.
Expect other drivers to see you and respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to parked cars to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for someone to step out or a car to pull out.
questions.explanation: Keep distance from parked cars. A person may step out without looking, or a driver may pull out without seeing you.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels of a vehicle follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space to turn right.

questions.question: A good driver should:

options.text: Focus only on the middle of the road.
Watch all around the car—sides, front, and back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch all around the car—sides, front, and back.
questions.explanation: Good drivers watch all around their vehicle. You need to know what is happening on all sides.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Disappear in blind spots or are too close for safe stopping and turning.
Have enough space to drive behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear in blind spots or are too close for safe stopping and turning.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots where cars disappear or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. These areas greatly increase crash risk.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with a blood alcohol level of:
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any amount of alcohol in your system will result in license suspension for two years.
